summary: Stahley Mountain's 1934 28-foot pole L-4 tower served the Aircraft Warning Service in 1942-43 and was removed or destroyed in the 1950s; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in the 1950s; sources disagree which, and none describes the site today

events.note: Colville Examiner item dated November 4, 1933 says a camp of 59 men was still finishing projects, including the Staley lookout station
28-foot pole tower with L-4 cab finished in 1934
Wendell Heide was at the station for a few days during an electric storm (item dated June 6, 1936); not a long-term staffing record
Aircraft Warning Service used the lookout; activated March 27, 1942
Aircraft Warning Service use ended; deactivated July 1, 1943
Mr. and Mrs. V.L. Stevens of Northport occupied the lookout (October 1944 item)
Register says removed in the 1950s; the year 1950 is a placeholder for the decade, not a recorded date
FireLookout.com and Will Hite say destroyed in the 1950s; the year 1950 is a placeholder for the decade
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on November 19, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower was removed in the 1950s; FireLookout.com and Will Hite say it was destroyed in that decade. No source explains how, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today or says whether it is reachable, so access is omitted. The 1950 event years are decade placeholders. The 1933 newspaper spells the name Staley; the brief and most sources use Stahley. No new photos found. Brief status gone and FFLOS registration date are confirmed; no corrections proposed.
